subject: Generation latency spike after A/B model swap - ClarityAI
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex@clarityai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClarityAI SRE <sre@clarityai.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:03Z
Subject: Immediate: generation latency spike since model swap

Hi Neha,

We just saw a sharp p95/p99 spike across our prod traffic after the model version swap that was rolled out at ~09:05. p95 went from ~180ms to ~1.9s and p99 is showing up around 3.4s. This is affecting several customer journeys (batch summarization and real-time chat).

Attached are a short perf snapshot and a few traces (trace ids 8f2a, 8f2b). Can you confirm whether the A/B rollout completed and whether there's a rollback option? We need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior SRE, ClarityAI

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20280315.tar.gz, trace-clarityai-20280315.json
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Barnes <alex@clarityai.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:25:18Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: generation latency spike since model swap

Thanks Alex — I’m escalating now and will coordinate a rollback if engineering confirms the new model variant is the cause. Looping Rishi (runtime), Lauren (CS lead) and Marissa (AM). Marissa, can you keep Alex posted on commercial/credit asks if we need to make concessions?

Rishi — can you take a look at the traces and confirm whether the A/B swap completed to 100% or if some routes are still on the old model? If rollback is the safest path please say so and we’ll request it.

-Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Barnes <alex@clarityai.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:33:42Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: generation latency spike since model swap

I’m looking. Initial findings: the rollout scheduled for today was an A/B swap from v3a (baseline) to v3b-quant at 09:00 UTC. Canary stepped 20% -> 100% between 09:05 and 09:12; control plane shows the traffic split reached 100% at 09:12.

Metrics summary (clarityai-prod):
- p50: 120ms -> 140ms (small change)
- p95: 180ms -> 1.9s (major regression)
- p99: 430ms -> 3.4s
- error rate: unchanged (~0.1%)
- throughput: steady

Preliminary hypothesis: v3b-quant introduces a different KV cache miss pattern or larger context kernel path that inflates tail latency under the production sequence-length mix. I’ve requested the full set of traces from the control plane; Alex’s traces match the spike (ids 8f2a/8f2b).

Immediate recommended action: throttle rollback the A/B split to 0% for v3b-quant (restore v3a to 100%) and keep canary paused. I can run the rollback if CS approves. Will attach quick rollback commands.

- Rishi
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: rollback-commands.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@clarityai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:41:05Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: generation latency spike since model swap

Alex — thanks for the quick signal. We’re authorizing a rollback to v3a while the engineering team investigates. Neha and I will own communication cadence.

Proposed immediate MAP (mutual action plan):
- 09:45: rollback traffic to v3a (Rishi)
- 10:00: validate p95/p99 across test routes (Rishi + Clarity SRE)
- 10:30: post-mortem and timeline for a fix + next canary plan (Redwood + Clarity)

If customers ask about credits we’ll triage after service is stable; please hold escalations to me and Neha.

-Marissa

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-15T09:48:30Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: generation latency spike since model swap

I pushed the rollback to the canary control plane at 09:46 UTC and set traffic-split v3b-quant -> 0%. Console output below (truncated):

> set-traffic --model-instance v3b-quant --percent 0 --env prod
> success: previous split 100% -> now 0% (completed 09:46:22 UTC)

I also increased the model concurrency soft-limit for Clarity’s project from 64 -> 80 while we validate; this should reduce queuing. Uploading a perf snapshot to the shared Drive.

Files uploaded: perf-snapshot-20280315.tar.gz (link in thread)

-Hannah
Production Ops
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Barnes <alex@clarityai.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T10:12:10Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: generation latency spike since model swap

Rollback completed, confirmed. Post-rollback metrics (clarityai-prod, sampled over 10m window):
- p50: 125ms
- p95: 190ms (back to baseline)
- p99: 480ms
- error rate: 0.12%

I’ve uploaded raw traces and a brief analysis to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-traces (includes trace ids 8f2a/8f2b and runtime profiler snapshots). Early kernel-level profiling shows a heavier multi-GEMM kernel path triggered by a longer kv-cache eviction chain in v3b-quant for sequences > 512. We will schedule a deeper investigation and consider a targeted quantization profile tweak.

JIRA ticket created: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/RDW-3491 (postmortem + regression fix).

-Rishi
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alex Barnes <alex@clarityai.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T16:32:10Z
Subject: Post-rollback update and exec summary — ClarityAI incident

Avery — quick summary for execs and next steps. Rolling into customer-facing follow-up and compensation discussion.

What happened: an A/B model swap (v3a -> v3b-quant) reached 100% traffic at ~09:12 UTC which produced a p95/p99 regression for ClarityAI. We executed an immediate rollback to v3a at 09:46; metrics returned to baseline by ~10:12. No data exposure or increase in error rate observed.

Impact: customer-facing latency regressions for critical flows; no request loss. Clarity has paused any automation that would reattempt the swap.

Actions taken:
- Ops rollback at 09:46 (Hannah)
- Increased concurrency soft-limit for customer while we validate
- Runtime team posted traces and initial analysis (Rishi)
- JIRA RDW-3491 opened for regression and kernel/kernel-selection tuning

Asks for execs:
- Approve a goodwill credit (proposed: 5% monthly usage credit) to ClarityAI to close the ticket while we complete the postmortem.
- If you’d like, engineering can prepare a short RCA for leadership review by EOD tomorrow.

We’ll keep this thread updated with the postmortem and a proposed safe-canary checklist to avoid repeat regressions.

-Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
